label: prop:jet-filtration-binding-extensive
title: The jet-filtration binding is extensive (monotone in body order)
html:
Proposition. The jet-filtration binding is extensive (monotone in body order)

Stated over \mathbb{R} (archimedean regime); the combinatorial content is a finite non-negative sum.

Proposition (extensivity of the body-order binding). Write the jet-filtration binding of conj:binding-manybody-eq-jet-filtration as

  B(A) \;=\; \sum_{n=2}^{A} \mathfrak{m}_e \, a_D^{(n)} \, w_n ,

with \mathfrak{m}_e \geq 0, and a_D^{(n)} \geq 0, w_n \geq 0 for every body order n. Then B is monotone non-decreasing in the body-order cutoff A:

  A \leq A' \;\Longrightarrow\; B(A) \leq B(A') ,

and it is strictly increasing whenever a new body order contributes positively: if \mathfrak{m}_e\, a_D^{(A+1)}\, w_{A+1} > 0 (and A+1 \geq 2), then B(A) < B(A+1).

Adding nucleon body orders can only increase binding. This is exactly the extensive behaviour the intensive rotation-phase reading \theta_\lambda = \arccos(\chi^\lambda/d_\lambda) structurally lacked — a bounded per-block phase cannot grow with the nucleon number A (see the failed one-parameter closure in probe_full_theta_binding.py). The body-order series supplies it, because each term \mathfrak{m}_e a_D^{(n)} w_n is a non-negative contribution and the number of terms grows with A.

The proof is elementary — monotonicity of a finite sum of non-negative terms over the nested index sets \{2,\ldots,A\} \subseteq \{2,\ldots,A'\}.

Scope (what is not asserted here). The three deeper inputs are carried as non-negativity/positivity hypotheses on a_D^{(n)} and w_n, not derived in this proposition:

  1. the super-exponential magnitude of the Seiberg–Witten period a_D^{(n)} = \oint_{\mathcal{S}_c}\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)} — the quantitative extensive channel;
  2. the non-abelian-Stokes identity a_D^{(n)} = \mathrm{lw}(n-1) (the mean quantum dimension; conjectural, with residue-sum form prop:sw-period-residue-sum);
  3. the per-atom residue weight w_n(K) (the \rho\cdot A scale rule, a q-difference recursion output).

What is established is the qualitative extensivity: given non-negative period and weight data, the body-order binding grows with A.

Status of (1)–(3) elsewhere in the corpus. Being carried as a hypothesis here is not the same as being open, and only one of the three now is. Item (2) is open: it is axiomatised as the §3b conjecture class QOU.Mass.NaStokesKeystone.ProlongationPeriodMeanQuantumDim, which has no instance. Item (1) is settled as a growth class — the period is super-exponential by the \surd-branch argument of the colour cubic, confirmed independently by the residue-sum route, and the object is identified as the q-deformed involution number T_q(n) = n\,\mathrm{lw}(n-1) \to I(n); what remains open there is the exact q-statistic, for which no q-holonomic recurrence exists at low depth. Note in particular that the falling factorial (1/2)_n is not a closed form for \mathrm{lw} — it outgrows it, and no constant geometric factor absorbs the difference. Item (3) is excluded rather than open: w_3 is a required boundary condition of a rank-2 problem, a scope-(b) result with its invariant cited (no_scalar_kernel_on_carrier).

The magnitude that matches experiment therefore depends on (1)–(3) as inputs, of which (2) is the one still to be derived. See 2026-08-29-jet-filtration-three-inputs-corpus-grep.md.
